summary: This annual survey covers institutional activity from July 1, 2011, through June 30, 2012, with institutions reporting their own undergraduate and graduate enrollment or instructional activity for that 12-month period. The unit of observation is the postsecondary institution, and the universe is eligible U.S. postsecondary institutions in the IPEDS reporting system, including institutions serving students through nontraditional calendars or short-term programs. The two tables provide complementary annual measures: unduplicated students served and instructional hours delivered.

The Completions survey is collected annually for activity from July 1, 2011, through June 30, 2012, and covers IPEDS institutions eligible to report postsecondary awards and programs. Its unit is the institution, with some tables adding program, award-level, or other category detail. The survey includes both awards conferred and students receiving awards, so those measures are not interchangeable.

Fall Enrollment reports students enrolled at participating postsecondary institutions during the fall: traditional academic calendars use October 15 or the institution’s official fall reporting date, while other or continuous-enrollment calendars count students enrolled at any time from August 1 through October 31. The observation unit is the institution, with tables containing one or more institution-level records at the relevant breakdown grain. Eligibility and coverage vary by table, including restrictions for four-year institutions, undergraduate students, and academic-year institutions; optional components may have incomplete institutional coverage.

The Finance component collects annual institutional financial data for the fiscal year ending in 2012, during the IPEDS Finance collection window following that fiscal year. The unit of observation is the postsecondary institution, and the universe is Title IV-participating institutions subject to IPEDS reporting; institutions report according to the accounting model and organizational type that apply to them. The survey covers institutional revenues, expenditures, assets, and liabilities, with separate forms for GASB public institutions, FASB institutions, and private for-profit institutions.

These tables report graduation and transfer outcomes as of August 31, 2012 for cohorts of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at eligible postsecondary institutions. The unit is an institution-level cohort/status record, with institutions and cohorts separated by sector and program-seeking population; the tables use different normal-time follow-up horizons and cohort years. Results are limited to the specified undergraduate cohorts and do not represent all enrolled students.

Human Resources data cover staff on institutional payroll as of November 1, with salary data for academic year 2012-13 and new-hire activity from July 1 through October 31. Records are institution-level and may contain multiple rows per institution, with each table using its own staff category or occupational key. Some tables are limited to degree-granting institutions with at least 15 full-time employees and related administrative offices; reporting race/ethnicity and gender, and the new-hire data, is optional in even-numbered years, so 2012 has incomplete coverage for those data.

These institution-level data were collected during the fall 2012 IPEDS cycle for academic year 2012-13. The universe is the institutions in the 2012 IPEDS universe; reporting is mandatory for institutions participating in Title IV federal student aid programs, with institution status and applicability identified in the data. Tables may cover active institutions and, where applicable, parent/child or multi-campus reporting arrangements.

Student Financial Aid is an institution-level collection covering aid awarded from July 1, 2011, through June 30, 2012; the 2011-12 data were collected during the winter reporting window (January 18–April 4, 2012). Its universe is Title IV-participating postsecondary institutions with undergraduate students, with counts and dollar amounts reported for defined undergraduate populations rather than individual students. Reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2012 (even) has data only from institutions that reported.
